observed: One lower semicircle with a horizontal flat diameter and a common interface hit at the center.
A vertical normal extends above and below the interface hit.
The incident straight trace enters from the lower left; a reflected straight ray leaves toward the lower right with an arrowhead.
A dashed grazing refracted ray extends right along the horizontal interface and ends in an arrowhead.
An upper-right quarter-angle arc is labelled beta = 90. Lower arcs are labelled alpha with subscript zero on the incident side and gamma on the reflected side.
No alphabetic endpoint names, material labels, numerical incidence angle, or index value are printed.
limits: Printed ray slopes are qualitative, not measured glass critical-angle values.
textBoundRequirements: This modern rendering explicitly represents the critical boundary: incidence equals the critical angle, refraction is grazing, not a supercritical transmitted beam.
A strictly greater incidence angle is necessary to remove propagation into the second medium; this figure must not conflate equality and strictly greater incidence.
The ideal transparent, nonabsorbing-interface energy limit is inherited from the prose; no measured energy percentage is added.
modernAdditions: Regularized rays use a representative glass geometry derived from the prose's approximate index example; no numerical incidence angle or index is printed.
English Air, Glass, Critical boundary and Modern schematic labels and tiny endpoint markers are modern additions.
The source beta label receives a degree symbol to make the already-given right angle explicit.

mappings.description: One lower semicylinder, horizontal interface, normal, lower-left incidence, lower-right reflection and dashed rightward grazing ray share one interface hit. All source relationships retained; slopes standardized, not measured.
Source lower alpha-zero and gamma arcs and upper-right beta equals 90 arc; degree-symbol normalization is modern, no other numerical angle added.
